title: Bounded completion of the row search
statement: Let $l\in\mathbb{N}$, let $pos,neg\in\{0,\ldots,l-1\}$ be distinct, and choose a Boolean input word, a family of rows of Boolean words indexed by natural numbers, two target words, natural numbers $N,W$, and a Boolean trailer. Suppose each word in each of the first $N$ rows has length at most $W$, and each target word has length at most $W$. There is a natural number $t\le N\bigl(l(5W+7)+2W+5\bigr)+1$ such that after $t$ steps the matcher is in its completed control, the candidate bank holds empty words if $N=0$ and otherwise row $N-1$, the stream and targets are unchanged, the cursor is at the length of the packed first $N$ rows, the clock is $N$, and the flags are the comparison results for rows $0$ through $N-1$ in order.
hypotheses_covered: Distinct coordinates $pos$ and $neg$ in the range of length $l$
Family of rows of Boolean words
Each word in each row with index less than $N$ has length at most $W$
Each target word has length at most $W$
replaced: For distinct coordinates, a row family with fields of length at most $W$ among the first $N$ rows, target words of length at most $W$, and a trailer, there is a time $t \le N(l(5W+7) + 2W + 5) + 1$ after which the matcher is in its completed control holding exactly the $N$ comparison flags in source-time order; the next row and the arbitrary tail are untouched, and at $N = 0$ only the silent stop executes.
